_about: Rates and assumptions behind the Value & ROI page. Defaults come from the Ballon TD market research (Oct 2026); basis says how solid each one is: Fact = sourced figure, Estimate = derived from sourced figures, Assumption = placeholder the client should replace with its own number. Amounts in US$. Edit them on Value > Assumptions or Library > Value assumptions.

assumptions.name: Display currency (units per US$)
assumptions.source: Amounts are entered in US$. Set the rate and the currency code (e.g. 3.6725 and AED) to show every figure in another currency.
assumptions.note: The unit column holds the currency code.

assumptions.name: Training cost per learning hour
assumptions.source: ATD State of the Industry 2025 (2024 data): cost per learning hour used US$165 (td.org)
assumptions.note: Applied to completed and attended training hours.

assumptions.name: Coaching cost per hour (preparation, session and reporting)
assumptions.source: Coaching at about US$1,800–4,500 per employee per year (BetterUp, third-party estimate, low confidence) over roughly 12–30 coaching hours

assumptions.name: Certification exam fee
assumptions.note: Counted for certifications achieved, scheduled or in progress.

assumptions.name: Hands-on lab seat
assumptions.source: Hack The Box Enterprise listed tier US$2,500 per seat per year (hackthebox.com/pricing)
assumptions.note: One seat per person with a lab collection assigned.

assumptions.name: Assessment and readiness reporting
assumptions.source: Quarterly Readiness Report package US$12k–20k per year for a 36-person team (research, part 6.2)

assumptions.name: Platform and executive dashboard
assumptions.source: Executive Cyber Workforce Dashboard package US$25k–45k per year (research, part 6.2); Immersive median US$44,250 (Vendr)
assumptions.note: Counted once per client in scope.

assumptions.name: Count participants' time as a cost
assumptions.source: Phillips ROI methodology counts participants' time away from work as a programme cost
assumptions.note: Training and coaching hours × the loaded hourly cost below.

assumptions.name: Loaded annual cost per employee
assumptions.source: Placeholder: replace with the client's average salary plus benefits for the people in scope (research, part 7 #3: salary band is not in the data model yet)
assumptions.note: Drives the value of capability gained and the cost of participants' time.

assumptions.name: Working hours per year
assumptions.source: Standard full-time year net of leave
assumptions.note: Loaded hourly cost = loaded annual cost ÷ working hours.

assumptions.name: Value of full role competence (share of loaded cost)
assumptions.source: Competency-based utility analysis (Phillips): one percentage point of role readiness is worth one percent of the role's loaded cost per year
assumptions.note: Lower it to be more conservative.

assumptions.name: External hire or replacement cost per role
assumptions.source: Placeholder: about 30% of the loaded cost (agency fee, vacancy and ramp-up). Replace with the client's cost per hire (research, part 7 #11)
assumptions.note: Used for internal fills and retention.

assumptions.name: Share of ready people who fill a role internally within 12 months
assumptions.source: Placeholder: confirm with the client's succession plan
assumptions.note: Applied to people ready now or in 6–12 months.

assumptions.name: Baseline annual attrition
assumptions.source: Placeholder: replace with the client's attrition for these roles (HRIS)

assumptions.name: Attrition reduction for programme participants
assumptions.source: LinkedIn Workplace Learning Report 2025: learning is the #1 retention strategy (qualitative); no published effect size. Replace with measured retention once 12 months of data exist (KPI K032)

assumptions.name: Share of improvement attributed to the programme
assumptions.source: Phillips ROI isolation step: credit the programme with only part of the measured change
